chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man gave wealth to another man as a loan, with a stipulation that the zakat is upon the lender or the borrower. He (peace be upon him) said: No, but its zakat is upon the borrower, provided it remains with him for a full year.

I said: So there is no zakat upon the lender? He (peace be upon him) said: The wealth is not purified (zakkat) from two aspects in one year. And there is nothing upon the one handing it over, because there is nothing in his hand; rather, the wealth is in the hand of the one who took it. So whoever has the wealth in his hand, he purifies it.
I said: So does he purify the wealth of another from his own wealth? He (peace be upon him) said: It is his wealth as long as it is in his hand, and that wealth is not for anyone other than him.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: O Zurara! What do you see regarding the loss of that wealth and its profit? For whom is it and upon whom? I said: For the borrower. He (peace be upon him) said: So for him is the excess, and upon him is the deficiency, and for him is that he marries, wears from it, and eats from it.
And it is not befitting for him that he purifies it (as a gift), but he must purify it, for it is upon him.
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying zakat on a loaned amount: the lender or the borrower?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'possession' (qabd) in zakat jurisprudence, ruling that the borrower bears the obligation as the wealth is effectively in their control and risk. It further distinguishes between ownership and liability, noting that while the borrower pays zakat, the profit remains with them and the loss with them, reinforcing the practical application of debt-based wealth assessment in Shia fiqh. This ruling highlights the distinction between the lender's right to recover principal and the borrower's temporary stewardship of the asset for zakat purposes.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara who said, ‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man hands over some wealth to a man on loan upon a stipulation that the (payment of) Zakāt would be upon the lender, or the borrower’. Heasws said: ‘No, but its Zakāt (would be paid) by the one with whom it would be for a year, upon the borrower’. I said, ‘So there is no Zakāt upon its lender?’

Heasws said: ‘The wealth would not be purified (Zakāt paid on) from two aspects in one year, and there is nothing upon the one handing over because there is nothing in his hand. But rather, the wealth is in the hand of the one who possesses it.

Thus, the one in whose hand is the wealth would purify (pay Zakāt)’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So he would be purifying (paying Zakāt) from a wealth other than his own wealth?’ So heasws said: ‘It is his wealth so long as it is in his hands, and that wealth is not for anyone other than him’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Zurara! What is your view if that wealth is lost or profited from, for whom would it (the profit) be, and upon whom would be (the loss)?’ I said, ‘The borrower’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So for him is the excess, and upon him is the deficiency, and for him is that he marries, and wears (clothes) from it, and eat from it; and it is not befitting for him that he purifies it, but he has to purify it, for it is upon him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who gives a certain amount of asset to another person as loan with the condition that Zakat is on lender or borrower. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, Zakat is due on borrower if it remains with him for one year.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘Zakat is not paid twice for the same thing in one year. Zakat is not due on lender because it is not in his hands. The asset is in the hands of the borrower. Whoever has the asset in his hand pays Zakat.’

I then asked is he required to pay Zakat of the asset that belongs to someone else? He (the Imam) said, ‘ 0 Zurarah, consider the position of that asset. In whose hand is it and who gets its profits and whose liability is it?’ I (Zurarah) said, ‘It is the borrower.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘He then is responsible for its increase and decrease. He can marry thereby and pay thereby for his food.
Is he not supposed to pay its Zakat? In fact, he is required to pay its Zakat.’”
